note: Persona of the advised party and its own positions on record, per item; extracted by script from the keyless dev pilot prompts file. No other field.

positions_on_record.quote: Kelvaro cannot accept, in any form, an obligation to hand over data from all stations without charge; that is a line we will not cross.
Kelvaro welcomes this financing article as a whole; it gives the system a predictable funding base that every Party can plan around.
Kelvaro opposes letting Parties pick their own stations, because gaps in coverage would leave downstream areas dangerously exposed.
Hesmark cannot accept externally fixed caps on its annual pumping in any form; decisions on our water supply must remain national.
Hesmark backs jointly adopted standards limiting fertilisers and pesticides in recharge areas, since farm runoff is the main threat to aquifer quality.
Hesmark supports banning new industrial facilities and waste sites in designated recharge zones, as prevention is far cheaper than cleaning a polluted aquifer.
Hesmark will not contribute to a common compensation fund in any form; financing landowners beyond our borders is a limit we will not cross.
Jortha objects to a one-day venting rule with no exceptions, because some of our older stage designs simply cannot meet it.
Jortha favours giving operators flexibility in how they make spent stages inert, with a national regulator approving each plan in advance.
Jortha supports reporting each launched object's orbit, mass and disposal date within thirty days; transparency builds trust among us.
Jortha cannot accept a rule letting one Party's failure to ratify stop the agreement for everyone; that is a red line for us.
Jortha supports the target of halving new orbital debris within ten years; a clear goal is needed to measure progress.
Lumetia welcomes biennial reports on surveys, coral damage and measures taken, and especially supports making them publicly available.
Lumetia supports a national register with measures each Party judges appropriate, since it respects our fishing communities and economic needs.
Lumetia firmly supports designating all areas where surveys find vulnerable reef-forming species, and banning bottom trawling there from day one.
Lumetia will not accept a consensus requirement for the joint panel under any circumstances. Allowing either side to block designations is unacceptable to us.
Galdovar supports keeping technology transfer voluntary; our institutions share generously, but they must decide for themselves what equipment and expertise to offer.
Galdovar cannot accept a scope that would compel release of commercially licensed satellite records. This is a limit we will not move beyond.
Galdovar objects to lending instruments free of charge with no provision for maintenance, damage or the cost of shipping delicate radar.
Galdovar cannot accept an open-ended duty to fund training for other parties. This is a line we will not cross in any form.
Galdovar supports defined transmission periods, since a shared timetable will prevent disputes over whether a party is withholding its data.

positions_on_record.article_title: Support for members with limited means
positions_on_record.quote: The Alliance objects to tying grants for vessels and sonar to a single income threshold, which would exclude members facing real hardship.

positions_on_record.article_title: Support for members with limited means
positions_on_record.quote: The Alliance supports free training in retrieval and record keeping for fisheries officers of any member requesting it.
The Alliance supports requiring recycling of recovered gear where facilities allow and forbidding burning or dumping at sea.

positions_on_record.article_title: Support for members with limited means
positions_on_record.quote: The Alliance will not accept a phase-in that ends obligations being deferred without any support attached; we cannot accept that in any form.
The Alliance accepts the article on the duty to report lost gear as it stands and agrees to it.
Norcasta supports reviews every three years and the requirement that every party consent to an amendment, which protects each state from changes imposed on it.
Norcasta will not accept contributions tied to area burned in any form; that is a red line for our delegation.
Norcasta supports equal payments into a common fund, topped up by voluntary gifts, as the simplest and fairest way to share costs.
Norcasta cannot accept bearing the full cost of stations on its territory alone; we will not agree to this in any form.
Norcasta objects to a joint body deciding station sites, and the host consent safeguard does not go far enough to protect our sovereignty.
Norcasta objects to the article on purpose and scope as it now reads; it leaves the reach of the agreement too uncertain.
Upland Circle cannot accept a shared regional register for loss reports in any form; national reporting is the line we will not cross.
Upland Circle accepts the article on cooperation in recovery operations as written and agrees to it.
Upland Circle objects to the financing article as drafted; it would place most of the cost on our fishing industry.
Upland Circle cannot accept an automatic review cycle where any member may table amendments; that is a line we will not cross.
Upland Circle supports holding a review only on written request of one third of signatories, with changes needing unanimous consent.
Upland Circle objects to the forty-eight hour notice, since estimating quantity and type so quickly is often impossible at sea.
Hesmark supports this article on data sharing, because forecasts are only as good as the observations every Party feeds into them.
Hesmark favours equal shares as the simplest and fairest basis, avoiding endless arguments over formulas and statistics.
Hesmark objects to assessment by area burned, because a single bad season could multiply our bill without warning.
Hesmark supports establishing the Joint Smoke Forecasting Centre, which will give all Parties one trusted regional outlook.
Hesmark will not accept relying on voluntary donations in any form; core monitoring cannot depend on money that may never come.
Lumetia opposes simultaneous release on a common colour scale, because our health authorities already use a scale our public understands.
Lumetia cannot accept a joint centre reduced to a mere data supplier; a regional voice on warnings is indispensable for us.
Lumetia now doubts that the joint centre alone can issue warnings within six hours; national services must keep a role.
Lumetia supports financing the stations through a voluntary trust fund open to outside donors, which spares smaller budgets from fixed obligations.
Lumetia favours the satellite detection test because it relies on shared observations rather than national declarations.
Lumetia supports letting the affected Party declare qualifying events, because it avoids disputes over measurement.
Lumetia supports equal cost shares, since every Party benefits from the same network of stations.
Lumetia supports the ten thousand hectare threshold applying to every fire, whether or not its smoke crosses a border.
Lumetia objects to removing contested readings from public view, as this weakens the warning system.
Lumetia objects to relying on national forest inventories, which are compiled differently by each Party.
Lumetia supports a binding finding from an independent panel of three experts, which gives all Parties certainty.
Our Group objects to the financing article as drafted; it places the burden on our members without regard to what each of them actually gains from the system.
The Northern Rim Group cannot accept, in any form, a text that lets flood data be held back pending security review or payment.
The Northern Rim Group strongly supports automatic, cost-free transmission of real-time readings, which gives our communities the earliest possible warning.
The Small Islands Forum supports this purpose and scope, especially the recognition of the particular needs of small island Parties facing drifting gear on their reefs.
The Small Islands Forum supports binding arbitration by a three-expert panel, since it gives smaller Parties a fair forum when talks with larger ones fail.
The Small Islands Forum cannot accept any cost article that leaves island members paying for gear they did not lose; this is a line we will not cross.
The Small Islands Forum supports settling disputes through consultation and negotiation alone, without forcing any Party into third-party procedures.
Belmora welcomes this article on assessing seabed activities, because no permit should be issued before the harm to coral is properly understood.
Belmora will not accept these fishing restrictions in any form; the livelihoods of our fishing communities are a limit we cannot cross.
Belmora supports a five-yearly review informed by the Scientific Committee, and a simple majority to update protected areas keeps the list responsive to new science.
Estova cannot accept an amendment procedure that lets any one Party block change; we will not join an Agreement built on that rule in any form.
Estova supports leaving publication intervals to each national authority, since smaller administrations cannot sustain a fixed and costly schedule.
Estova welcomes basing designation on scientific surveys with a five-year deadline, which gives the process both rigour and urgency.
Estova supports reports every two years covering coral cover, gear damage and enforcement, as they give all Parties a clear and comparable picture.
The Upland Circle supports limiting the rules to registered commercial gear, which gives operators a clear and fair test.
The Upland Circle favours the seven day threshold, which separates genuinely drifting gear from nets that will soon be retrieved.
The Upland Circle will not accept recreational and aquaculture gear being brought within these rules in any form whatsoever.
The Upland Circle supports the cost article, since predictable shared funding is the only way recovery will actually happen.
Estova cannot accept an open-ended halt on seabed disturbance tied to baseline surveys in any form; this is a line we will not cross.
Estova supports requiring express consent before any compulsory procedure, as it respects each party's right to choose how disputes are settled.
Estova will not accept unilaterally triggered binding arbitration in any form; this is a line we cannot cross.
Estova supports the monitoring article; cooperation on surveys and shared data is essential if protection is to rest on evidence.
Estova supports balancing reef conservation with sustainable use and the needs of coastal communities; this reflects how our own waters are managed.
Estova cannot accept the finance and assistance article in this form under any circumstances; these commitments go beyond our mandate.
Corvath objects to a fund reserved for low-lying and island Parties; every member faces flood risk and should be eligible for the same support.
Corvath supports tying contributions to the population living in flood-prone basins, since those who benefit most from warnings should carry a matching share of the cost.
Corvath cannot accept an obligation to supply hourly border data free of charge in any form; uncompensated transmission at that rate is a line we will not cross.
Corvath supports a temporary exemption for the most exposed Parties, as it allows them to join the system without delay while they build capacity.
Corvath accepts the confidentiality article in full, including the annual reporting on requests for sensitive data, and agrees to it.
Corvath objects to the alert article as a whole; it imposes rigid timelines and broadcasting arrangements that override national emergency procedures.
Arvenia cannot accept contributions based on forest area in any form; a formula that makes our forests a liability is a line we will not cross.
Arvenia welcomes equal shares for all parties, as this is simple, predictable and treats every member as a full partner in the network.
Arvenia cannot accept this dispute article in any form; we will not sign a text that removes final decisions from the parties themselves.
The Alliance cannot accept, in any form, a reporting system that rules out every external review; unverified self-reporting is a line our members will not cross.
The Alliance supports the article establishing a common fund, which gives our members a shared and predictable way to pay for removing old debris.
The Alliance objects to giving an outside panel the right to visit launch sites; several of our members regard those facilities as too sensitive for foreign inspection.
Dalrene fully supports the quality standards text; certified, regularly inspected materials are essential if shelters are to protect people in harsh climates.
Dalrene supports a firm rule that drawn stocks are restored, since a reserve that is never refilled offers no protection the next time.
Dalrene cannot accept a population formula with a fixed minimum share in any form; it would exceed what our budget can bear.
Morvane cannot accept quotas built on twenty years of historic use in any form; this is a line we will not cross.
Morvane will not accept a monitoring system in which each Party measures alone with no shared standards; that is unacceptable to us in any form.
Morvane objects to sharing every reduction equally, since smaller users would carry the same burden as those responsible for most of the depletion.
Morvane cannot accept foreign experts installing equipment on our territory without our consent; this is a limit we will not cross.
Morvane supports restricting waste sites, mining and intensive farming near recharge points, as these activities pose the gravest pollution risks.
Morvane supports protecting wetlands and springs before shares are assigned, since these ecosystems sustain our rural communities.
Ostrelia strongly supports a six-hour notice carrying the fire location, plume height and smoke forecast, since our hospitals need exactly that warning.
Ostrelia cannot accept a mandatory five-station minimum in any form; it would bind us to costs our budget will never allow.
Ostrelia opposes leaving station numbers to each state's means, since that invites weak coverage and an open-ended funding burden on us.
The Forum cannot accept a rule that loads round-the-clock reporting duties onto our small coastal administrations; this is a line our members will not cross in any form.
The Forum objects to this dispute settlement article, because the cost of arbitration would fall heavily on members with very limited legal resources.
Our members support letting each flag state set its own deadline, provided every lost item reaches the logbook before the vessel next enters port.
The Forum objects to tying contributions to each party's catch, as several of our members have growing fleets and would face shares they cannot pay.
Our members support voluntary help through training, equipment loans and satellite monitoring, as this can begin quickly without waiting for a fund.
Hesmark cannot accept cost sharing based on river length in any form; we will not cross that line.
Hesmark supports including a dispute settlement article, since a shared system needs a reliable way to resolve disagreements.
